title: Ocean Currents in 60 Seconds

endcard.line: Footage: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (public domain); Ocean Observatories Initiative (public domain)

segments.say: Why are some desert coasts foggy, while western Europe stays mild in winter? The answer is rivers inside the sea.
Ocean currents are huge flows of water moving in a definite direction. They are set going by the Sun's heat, the wind, gravity and the Coriolis force.
Waves are different. In a wave the water mostly stays put, and only the wave moves on. In a current, the water itself travels.

anim.title: The Coriolis turn
items: Big loops form in every ocean basin

segments.say: Because the Earth spins, moving water turns right in the northern hemisphere and left in the southern. That bends currents into giant loops in every ocean.

left.title: Warm currents
items: east coasts, low and middle latitudes

right.title: Cold currents
items: west coasts, low and middle latitudes

segments.say: Warm currents carry tropical water towards the poles. Cold currents bring polar water towards the equator, often along the west coasts of continents, where they bring fog but little rain.

anim.below: of ocean water is in surface currents

segments.say: Surface currents hold only about a tenth of the ocean's water. The other nine-tenths moves slowly in the deep.
Where warm and cold currents meet, the water mixes, and you find the world's best fishing grounds. Remember that link for GS One.

sources: NCERT Class 11, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, ch. 13 (Movements of Ocean Water): definition of currents vs waves; primary forces (solar heating, wind, gravity, Coriolis); Coriolis turns water right in the north, left in the south, making large circular currents; surface currents about 10% of ocean water, deep currents 90%; cold currents on west coasts and warm on east coasts in low and middle latitudes; west coasts bordered by cool water have fog but are arid; west coasts in middle and higher latitudes bordered by warm water have a marine climate; best fishing grounds in mixing zones
NOAA Ocean Service, 'What is the global ocean conveyor belt?': deep circulation driven by temperature and salinity

quiz.q: In the northern hemisphere, the Coriolis force turns moving water to the…
quiz.why: Right in the northern hemisphere, left in the southern.

quiz.q: About what share of ocean water moves in surface currents?
quiz.why: Surface currents hold about a tenth; deep currents hold the other nine-tenths.

quiz.q: Where are the world's best fishing grounds usually found?
options: In the middle of warm currents
Where warm and cold currents mix
quiz.why: The video ends on the mixing zones of warm and cold currents.

reviewNote: Facts were read against NCERT Class 11 Fundamentals of Physical Geography ch. 13 and NOAA Ocean Service's conveyor-belt page. The NASA flow visualisation shows coastlines but no national borders; crop to open ocean and check before publishing. Moving facts: none known.
